kata.name: Visitor-as-sum-type above-floor: five-variant legacy visitor vs a sampled scripted dispatch test
kata.series_verdict: survived (pre-registered: exact enumeration over the finite variant domain names the shadowed, derivable, and newly-uncovered handler classes the sampled test does not; F1/F2 are parity)

expected.detail: remove `visit_num` (missing visitor method); kind=num is uncovered -> underconstraint (hypothesized)
add a second `add` registration and declare `DeclaredDisjoint` (duplicate visitor); the add input is shared -> violation (executed)
insert a broad (num OR str) registration before `visit_str` (shadowed handler); `visit_str` is dead under PriorityOrder -> redundant (executed)
re-register `num` as literal_scope AND arith_scope with dispatch preserved (derivable handler); `visit_num` is derivable -> redundant (executed)
add the `div` variant to the AST instance with no visitor rule (missing-variant coverage) -> underconstraint (hypothesized)

comparison.conventional_baseline: prototype/visitor_sum_types_baseline.py --assert: a scripted dispatch test over the pre-registered sample {num, add, neg}, the arithmetic nodes the legacy interpreter's suite exercised. It catches F1 (sample:num:missing) and F2 (sample:add:ambiguous:visit_add|visit_add_legacy); it misses F3 (str unsampled), F4 (dispatch preserved on every variant), and F5 (div unsampled).
unique_detections: F3 shadowed handler: `visit_str` is dead under PriorityOrder (reducing [literal_scope]); baseline sampled {num, add, neg} -> 0 detections
F4 derivable handler: `visit_num` = R(literal_scope) ∩ R(arith_scope), dispatch preserved on every variant; baseline sampled {num, add, neg} -> 0 detections
F5 missing-variant coverage: kind = "div" (input 5) has no rule; baseline sampled {num, add, neg} -> 0 detections

expressibility_gap.invariant: visitor method bodies compute the interpretation
expressibility_gap.why: the rule presentation's action is an opaque string; the lens proves every variant reaches a named action, never that the action's implementation returns the correct value

expressibility_gap.invariant: runtime class identity derived from state, not a declared `kind` column
expressibility_gap.why: X must be a finite product of typed attribute columns; identity computed from state is outside the declared attribute alphabet

expressibility_gap.invariant: double dispatch over (node kind x visitor type)
expressibility_gap.why: the rule presentation has one domain and one action function; two visitors are two documents with no cross-visitor consistency check

discrepancies: The baseline arm is a sampled scripted test by design. A conventional exhaustive dispatch test (one assertion per variant) would reach parity on the behavioral face of F1, F2, F3, and F5; it would not name the dead-rule structure in F3 nor the behavior-preserving derivability in F4. The unique set is the sampling gap plus structural redundancy, never a detection-rate win.

F4's derivable handler preserves dispatch on every variant, so its unique detection is a structural redundancy claim; a purely behavioral conventional test cannot distinguish it from ordinary priority dispatch.
procedure: 1. Declare the five-variant legacy visitor table and bind kind={num,str,add,mul,neg}; the lens reports zero findings.
2. Freeze the sampled scripted dispatch test at {num, add, neg} before injecting faults and run the baseline with --assert.
3. Inject F1 (missing num), F2 (duplicate add + DeclaredDisjoint), F3 (broad num OR str before str), F4 (derivable num, behavior preserved), F5 (div variant added to the AST with no rule).
4. Execute catherine rules on each fault and map every finding to the pre-registered class.
5. Unique = probe findings on faults the sampled baseline did not name: F3, F4, F5 -> 3; verdict survived (executed baseline arm).
